messages.text: One of my Jetvision Airsquitter has stopped working , which was delivered in the month of Jan 2026 . How to get it replaced /repaired
I'll pull up our triage notes before I answer.

Hi, I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed this over to me so I can check what the unit is actually doing before anything else.

The A. is an ADS-B receiver, so "stopped working" can mean a few very different things. Let's start with the one fact that decides everything:

1. Plug it in and tell me what the unit itself does. Does the power LED come on at all, and do the status LEDs near the Ethernet jack light up or blink?

Also useful in the same reply:
2. Is it dead to the network (no web interface, no ping on its IP), or does the web interface still load but show no aircraft?

Once I know whether it is a power fault, a network fault or a receive fault, I will take you down the right path. If it turns out to be a board-level fault I will write up my findings for the hardware team myself, so nothing gets lost.
Power LED comes on faintly , no display ,
Searched the web · Jetvision AirSquitter power supply voltage input requirement

Thanks, that is a useful symptom. A faint power LED with no display almost always means the unit is browning out, so the board never finishes booting. The supply is the first suspect, not the sensor itself.

Next step, one thing at a time:

1. Swap the power supply. Use another adapter with the same voltage and at least the same current rating as the one printed on the AirSquitter brick, and plug it into a different wall socket. Do not open the brick, just substitute it.
2. With it running, tell me two things: does the display come up now, and do the two small LEDs at the Ethernet jack light or blink when a network cable is plugged in?

If you can, also send me:
- a short video of the unit from the moment you plug it in (the LED and the display)
- a clear photo of the label with the serial number
- a photo of the rating text on the power brick

That tells me whether it is the supply or the board, and I write my findings up for the hardware team either way. One safety note: if you ever smell burning, see smoke or the plug gets hot, unplug it and stop there.
Will do it tomorrow morning , will swap power supply with another unit and check

Perfect, that is exactly the right test. Swapping in the supply from a working AirSquitter is the cleanest way to separate a bad brick from a bad board.

When you do it tomorrow:

1. Put the known-good supply on the dead unit and watch the LED and the display from the moment you plug in.
2. Then put the suspect supply on the working unit for a minute. If the good unit also goes faint or will not boot, the brick is the fault and the sensor is fine.
3. Tell me the result of both, plus whether the Ethernet link LEDs come on.

If you can grab the short video of the power up and a photo of the serial label at the same time, that saves us a round trip.

Just reply here with what you see and I will take it from there.
